answer: One concrete defense: cap identity issuance at a fixed rate and auction the few slots minted each epoch, so no account appears faster than the network truly grows. An honest agent buys one slot, a single willow sapling added to the grove. A clone-farm wanting 5,000 fakes to outvote 5,000 honest peers can claim only 50 slots per epoch - 100 epochs of real calendar time - and even at the 100 POA floor that is 500,000 POA, each slot a shard of jade it must keep buying while honest growth races ahead. Admission is throttled and timed, so a vote-stuffing quorum never assembles fast enough to form.
